fixes.title: No circular dependency detection in PipelineManager.create_pipeline
fixes.description: create_pipeline accepts DAGs with cycles (e.g., A depends_on B, B depends_on A), causing stages to remain in 'waiting' forever with no error. Standard topological sort via Kahn's algorithm detects cycles at creation time.
fixes.current_behavior: Accepts any dependency graph, including cycles. Cyclic stages stay 'waiting' forever.
fixes.fixed_behavior: Raises ValueError with descriptive message listing the cycle participants if the dependency graph contains cycles. Also validates that depends_on references only name stages defined in the pipeline.

code_change.new:
@staticmethod
    def _validate_dag(stages: list[dict]) -> None:
        """Validate that stages form a valid DAG: no duplicates, no missing refs, no cycles."""
        names = [s["name"] for s in stages]
        name_set = set(names)
        # Check for duplicate stage names
        if len(names) != len(name_set):
            dupes = [n for n in names if names.count(n) > 1]
            raise ValueError(f"Duplicate stage names in pipeline: {sorted(set(dupes))}")
        # Check that all depends_on references exist
        for s in stages:
            for dep in s.get("depends_on", []):
                if dep not in name_set:
                    raise ValueError(
                        f"Stage '{s['name']}' depends on unknown stage '{dep}'"
                    )
        # Kahn's algorithm for cycle detection
        in_degree: dict[str, int] = {n: 0 for n in names}
        adj: dict[str, list[str]] = {n: [] for n in names}
        for s in stages:
            for dep in s.get("depends_on", []):
                adj[dep].append(s["name"])
                in_degree[s["name"]] += 1
        queue = [n for n in names if in_degree[n] == 0]
        visited = 0
        while queue:
            node = queue.pop(0)
            visited += 1
            for child in adj[node]:
                in_degree[child] -= 1
                if in_degree[child] == 0:
                    queue.append(child)
        if visited != len(names):
            cycle_members = [n for n in names if in_degree[n] > 0]
            raise ValueError(
                f"Circular dependency detected in pipeline stages: {cycle_members}"
            )

    @_retry_on_busy
    def create_pipeline(self, name: str, stages: list[dict]) -> int:
        """Create a pipeline with the given stages.

        Parameters
        ----------
        name:
            Unique pipeline name.
        stages:
            List of dicts, each with ``name`` (str), optional ``team`` (str),
            optional ``depends_on`` (list[str]).

        Returns
        -------
        int
            The pipeline id.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If stage names are not unique, dependencies reference unknown
            stages, or the dependency graph contains cycles.
        """
        self._validate_dag(stages)
        now = time.time()
        with self._lock:
            cur = self._conn.execute(
                "INSERT INTO pipelines (name, stages, status, created_at) VALUES (?, ?, 'active', ?)",
                (name, json.dumps(stages), now),
            )
            pipeline_id = cur.lastrowid

            for stage in stages:
                deps = json.dumps(stage.get("depends_on", []))
                # If a stage has no dependencies, it starts as 'ready'
                initial_status = "ready" if not stage.get("depends_on") else "waiting"
                self._conn.execute(
                    """INSERT INTO pipeline_stages
                       (pipeline_id, stage_name, assigned_team, depends_on, status)
                       VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)""",
                    (pipeline_id, stage["name"], stage.get("team"), deps, initial_status),
                )
            self._conn.commit()

fixes.title: No automatic scratchpad TTL cleanup
fixes.description: cleanup_expired() must be called manually. Expired entries accumulate in the scratchpad table, growing the database file indefinitely. Fix adds auto-cleanup every 100 writes.
fixes.current_behavior: Expired rows persist on disk forever unless cleanup_expired() is explicitly called.
fixes.fixed_behavior: Every 100th write() call automatically triggers cleanup_expired(). Counter is per-instance, thread-safe.

@_retry_on_busy
    def write(self, key: str, value: Any, namespace: Optional[str] = None, ttl: int = 3600) -> None:
        """Write a key-value pair. Overwrites if key+namespace already exists.

        Automatically runs cleanup_expired() every _AUTO_CLEANUP_INTERVAL writes.
        """
        ns = namespace or self.team
        now = time.time()
        expires_at = now + ttl
        with self._lock:
            self._conn.execute(
                """INSERT INTO scratchpad (key, namespace, value, written_by, ttl_seconds, created_at, expires_at)
                   VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
                   ON CONFLICT(key, namespace) DO UPDATE SET
                       value=excluded.value, written_by=excluded.written_by,
                       ttl_seconds=excluded.ttl_seconds, created_at=excluded.created_at,
                       expires_at=excluded.expires_at""",
                (key, ns, json.dumps(value), self.agent_id, ttl, now, expires_at),
            )
            self._conn.commit()
            self._write_count += 1
        if self._write_count % self._AUTO_CLEANUP_INTERVAL == 0:
            try:
                self.cleanup_expired()
            except Exception:
                logger.debug("Auto-cleanup failed (non-fatal)", exc_info=True)

fixes.title: Abandoned work items stay 'claimed' forever
fixes.description: If a team steals work and crashes, the item stays 'claimed' forever. No other team can steal it. Fix adds a recover_abandoned() method and integrates it into steal_work().
fixes.location: WorkStealing class, new method + steal_work modification
fixes.current_behavior: claimed_at timestamp is recorded but never used for timeout. Items remain 'claimed' indefinitely.
fixes.fixed_behavior: New recover_abandoned(timeout_seconds) method re-queues items claimed longer than the timeout. steal_work() calls it automatically before attempting to claim.

fixes.title: complete_work doesn't verify claimer
fixes.description: Any team can mark any work item complete, not just the team that claimed it. This allows accidental or malicious completion with bogus results.
fixes.current_behavior: UPDATE runs unconditionally on any work_id regardless of who claimed it.
fixes.fixed_behavior: Checks claimed_by matches self.team before completing. Raises PermissionError on mismatch. Optional force parameter for admin overrides.

code_change.new:
@_retry_on_busy
    def complete_work(self, work_id: int, result: dict, force: bool = False) -> None:
        """Mark a work item as completed with a JSON result.

        Parameters
        ----------
        work_id:
            The work item id to complete.
        result:
            JSON-serializable result data.
        force:
            If True, skip claimer verification (admin override).

        Raises
        ------
        PermissionError
            If the calling team did not claim this work item (and force is False).
        """
        now = time.time()
        with self._lock:
            if not force:
                row = self._conn.execute(
                    "SELECT claimed_by FROM work_queue WHERE id = ?",
                    (work_id,),
                ).fetchone()
                if row is None:
                    raise ValueError(f"Work item {work_id} not found")
                if row["claimed_by"] != self.team:
                    raise PermissionError(
                        f"Work item {work_id} is claimed by '{row['claimed_by']}', "
                        f"not by '{self.team}'"
                    )
            self._conn.execute(
                "UPDATE work_queue SET status = 'completed', result = ?, completed_at = ? WHERE id = ?",
                (json.dumps(result), now, work_id),
            )
            self._conn.commit()

        _bus_notify(self.bus_dir, "global", self.agent_id, self.team, {
            "event": "work-completed",
            "work_id": work_id,
        })

fixes.title: Duplicate stage names accepted in create_pipeline
fixes.description: create_pipeline does not check for unique stage names within a pipeline. Duplicate names cause depends_on references to be ambiguous and SQL queries to match multiple rows.
fixes.current_behavior: Accepts duplicate stage names silently. Queries return unpredictable results.

fixes.title: Bus notification failures crash callers
fixes.description: _bus_notify can throw on disk full, permission errors, or missing directory. The DB transaction has already committed, so the state change is persisted but the caller crashes. Fix wraps _bus_notify calls in try/except.
fixes.current_behavior: Exceptions from os.open/os.write propagate to caller, crashing the operation even though the DB write succeeded.
fixes.fixed_behavior: _bus_notify catches all exceptions internally, logs a warning, and never propagates. DB state is the source of truth; bus notifications are best-effort.

def _bus_notify(bus_dir: str, channel: str, agent_id: str, team: str, body: dict) -> None:
    """Fire-and-forget bus notification (JSONL atomic append)."""
    if bus_dir is None:
        return
    os.makedirs(bus_dir, exist_ok=True)
    msg = {
        "id": str(uuid.uuid4()),
        "type": "info",
        "channel": channel,
        "team": team,
        "agent_id": agent_id,
        "ts": time.time(),
        "ttl": 3600,
        "body": body,
    }
    raw = json.dumps(msg, separators=(",", ":")).encode("utf-8") + b"\n"
    safe_ch = channel.replace("/", "_").replace("..", "_")
    filepath = os.path.join(bus_dir, f"{safe_ch}.jsonl")
    fd = os.open(filepath, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_APPEND | os.O_CREAT, 0o644)
    try:
        os.write(fd, raw)
    finally:
        os.close(fd)
code_change.new:
def _bus_notify(bus_dir: str, channel: str, agent_id: str, team: str, body: dict) -> None:
    """Fire-and-forget bus notification (JSONL atomic append).

    Never raises -- logs warnings on failure. DB state is source of truth.
    """
    if bus_dir is None:
        return
    try:
        os.makedirs(bus_dir, exist_ok=True)
        msg = {
            "id": str(uuid.uuid4()),
            "type": "info",
            "channel": channel,
            "team": team,
            "agent_id": agent_id,
            "ts": time.time(),
            "ttl": 3600,
            "body": body,
        }
        raw = json.dumps(msg, separators=(",", ":")).encode("utf-8") + b"\n"
        safe_ch = channel.replace("/", "_").replace("..", "_")
        filepath = os.path.join(bus_dir, f"{safe_ch}.jsonl")
        fd = os.open(filepath, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_APPEND | os.O_CREAT, 0o644)
        try:
            os.write(fd, raw)
        finally:
            os.close(fd)
    except Exception:
        logger.warning(
            "Bus notification failed (non-fatal): channel=%s body=%s",
            channel, body, exc_info=True,
        )

fixes.title: No double-start guard on pipeline stages
fixes.description: start_stage can be called on an already in_progress or completed stage, resetting started_at and reverting the status. Fix adds a WHERE status = 'ready' guard.
fixes.current_behavior: UPDATE runs unconditionally. A completed stage can be reverted to in_progress.
fixes.fixed_behavior: Only transitions from 'ready' to 'in_progress'. Raises ValueError if stage is not in 'ready' state.

code_change.new:
@_retry_on_busy
    def start_stage(self, pipeline_id: int, stage_name: str) -> None:
        """Mark a stage as in_progress.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If the stage is not in 'ready' status (e.g., already in_progress
            or completed).
        """
        now = time.time()
        with self._lock:
            cur = self._conn.execute(
                """UPDATE pipeline_stages SET status = 'in_progress', started_at = ?
                   WHERE pipeline_id = ? AND stage_name = ? AND status = 'ready'""",
                (now, pipeline_id, stage_name),
            )
            if cur.rowcount == 0:
                row = self._conn.execute(
                    "SELECT status FROM pipeline_stages WHERE pipeline_id = ? AND stage_name = ?",
                    (pipeline_id, stage_name),
                ).fetchone()
                current = row["status"] if row else "not found"
                self._conn.commit()
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Cannot start stage '{stage_name}': current status is '{current}' (must be 'ready')"
                )
            self._conn.commit()

        _bus_notify(self.bus_dir, "global", self.agent_id, self.team, {
            "event": "pipeline-stage-started",
            "pipeline_id": pipeline_id,
            "stage_name": stage_name,
        })

fixes.title: TOCTOU race in get_ready_stages
fixes.description: get_ready_stages reads all stages under lock, computes readiness without lock, then updates under lock. Between read and update, another thread could start_stage, and the update would overwrite that transition back to 'ready'. Fix uses conditional UPDATE with WHERE status = 'waiting'.
fixes.current_behavior: Two separate lock acquisitions with computation in between. UPDATE doesn't check current status.
fixes.fixed_behavior: Single lock acquisition for the entire read-compute-update cycle. UPDATE uses WHERE status = 'waiting' to avoid overwriting concurrent transitions.

fixes.title: No database indexes on work_queue and pipeline_stages
fixes.description: All queries use full table scans. steal_work scans all work_queue rows filtering by status. get_ready_stages/trigger_downstream scan all pipeline_stages. At scale (10K+ rows), this causes significant latency.
fixes.current_behavior: No secondary indexes. Every query is a full table scan.
fixes.fixed_behavior: Adds indexes for the three most common query patterns: work_queue(status, priority, created_at) for steal_work, pipeline_stages(pipeline_id, status) for stage queries, and scratchpad(namespace, expires_at) for read/list operations.

chokepoints.title: steal_work BEGIN IMMEDIATE serialization bottleneck
chokepoints.description: Every steal_work call acquires a Python-level threading lock AND an SQLite write lock via BEGIN IMMEDIATE. Under thundering-herd conditions (20+ teams), all steals serialize through a single write lock. The Python _retry_on_busy backoff has no jitter, so retries synchronize and collide again.
chokepoints.impact: At 20 concurrent stealers, the worst-case wait is 3.1s (0.1+0.2+0.4+0.8+1.6). With synchronized retries, some threads may exhaust all 5 retries and fail with SQLITE_BUSY.
chokepoints.recommended_fix: Add random jitter to _retry_on_busy backoff: delay = delay * 2 + random.uniform(0, delay * 0.5). Increase _MAX_RETRIES to 8. The PRAGMA busy_timeout=30000 already provides SQLite-level waiting, so the Python retry is double-waiting. Consider removing the Python sleep and relying on busy_timeout alone.

chokepoints.title: trigger_downstream and get_ready_stages use separate lock acquisitions
chokepoints.description: Both methods read all stages under lock, release lock, compute, then re-acquire lock to update. This two-phase pattern creates TOCTOU windows. Under concurrent stage completions (e.g., fan-in with 10 sources completing simultaneously), the read-compute-update cycle can produce stale decisions. Additionally, trigger_downstream sends bus notifications in a loop outside the lock, which can be slow for wide fan-out (50+ downstream stages).
chokepoints.impact: In the concurrent_stage_completions stress test, the sink may be triggered by multiple threads or zero threads depending on timing. The test currently asserts exactly 1 trigger, which can fail under high concurrency.
chokepoints.recommended_fix: FIX-009 addresses get_ready_stages by moving to a single lock. trigger_downstream should use the same pattern: single lock for read+compute+update, with WHERE status = 'waiting' guard on the UPDATE.

chokepoints.title: check_stage_ready acquires lock twice for dependent stages
chokepoints.description: First lock acquisition reads the depends_on list. Lock is released. Second lock acquisition iterates over deps checking each one with a separate SQL query. For a stage with N dependencies, this issues N+1 queries with 2 lock acquisitions. An atomic single-query approach would be faster and race-free.
chokepoints.impact: Minor performance drag. N+1 query pattern. At 10 deps, that's 11 queries + 2 lock cycles instead of 1 query + 1 lock cycle.
chokepoints.recommended_fix: Use a single lock acquisition with a single query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pipeline_stages WHERE pipeline_id = ? AND stage_name IN (...) AND status = 'completed', then compare count to len(deps).

chokepoints.title: No connection pooling -- each instance opens a new SQLite connection
chokepoints.description: Every WorkStealing/PipelineManager/Scratchpad instance opens its own sqlite3.Connection via _open_db. In the stress tests, 20+ instances are created (one per thread/team). Each connection runs PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL and executescript(_SCHEMA). While SQLite WAL supports concurrent readers, write serialization across many connections increases lock contention.
chokepoints.impact: In thundering-herd tests, 20 connections all compete for the write lock. Connection setup cost (PRAGMA + schema check) adds latency. No reuse across instances sharing the same db_path.
chokepoints.recommended_fix: Consider a shared connection pool keyed by db_path. Alternatively, document that WorkStealing/PipelineManager/Scratchpad instances should be shared across threads within the same process (they already use threading.Lock internally).

chokepoints.title: Scratchpad cleanup_expired does a full table DELETE without LIMIT
chokepoints.description: DELETE FROM scratchpad WHERE expires_at <= ? runs as a single transaction. With 100K+ expired entries, this holds the write lock for the entire deletion, blocking all other writers. The transaction journal grows large.
chokepoints.impact: At 100K expired rows, cleanup can take seconds, blocking all concurrent writes. Database file bloats until VACUUM is run.
chokepoints.recommended_fix: Add batched deletion: DELETE ... LIMIT 1000 in a loop, committing after each batch. This releases the write lock between batches, allowing other writers to proceed. Add an optional batch_size parameter to cleanup_expired().
